title: How many Triangles for a Tree?
author: TheUsualGuy666
selftext:
I'm making a top-down ARPG game like V Rising. I wonder how many triangles each tree should have?

I use Google AI ( I know, I know...) and it says it should be 3-6k triangles but when I use meshy to render it they come out horribly... anyways is 3-6k the approximate amount for my trees?

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
Generally speaking you will have to come up with your own guidelines for how many triangles. 

You can do estimates based on the triangle size on-screen. Like, “how many pixels across is my triangle, when rendered?” Go for like 10 or 15 pixels across. Do the math based on resolution and the size of the tree on-screen.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
You need to ask a few things:

1. What's my engine?  
2. What's my target audience?  
And then you can ask:  
3. What's my Poly budget?  
4. How many of this object are going to be on the screen at one time, and how important is it to maintain fidelity?  
5. Can the player zoom in?

  
Your target polys for trees might range anywhere from 500 to 10k depending on a number of factors. VRising trees remind me of Skyrim trees, wh ich had around 1300 tris. Other mods which added HD trees  (makes a lot more sense in a first person game where trees are 90% of the environmental fidelity) you were looking at 5-10k. If you're not rotating the camera around you can make some very good looking trees with 1000 tris with good quad masks for leaves and 99% of your poly budget dedicated to the trunk/branch structure. If a tree is a bit sharper at one edge than another it's not like a cheek or something where you might notice. 

So yeah... without knowing more about your project I'd personally target 1000-1500 tris, but if you are building it for Three.JS and trying to have hundreds of trees on screen at once I'd push it lower and go for a true low poly style. But if Unity or Unreal 1500 tris is nothing, even animated, and should serve you well. I don't think Meshy can make that though, especially if it's including the leaves. Astra could probably do so with blender though, and you can likely find available assets --- or maybe Tripo will be able to produce low enough polys on it. Probably. Depends on the ref.
